Messages.Author: Kushiel
Messages.Body:
1) Faceless Night's superior wording confuses me. If I call Domain
Challenge with a vampire who has OBF, and that vampire plays Faceless
Night at superior and sneaks past a vampire of my prey's, does my
prey's vampire tap before the referendum or after it?

2) I have a Slaughterhouse in play and bleed successfully. I play
Scrying of Secrets and look at the top seven cards in my prey's
library. If I tap a Slaughterhouse now to discard the top two, do I
then look at the next two (thereby keeping seven in my hand)?

John Eno

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Kushiel wrote:
> 1) Faceless Night's superior wording confuses me. If I call Domain
> Challenge with a vampire who has OBF, and that vampire plays Faceless
> Night at superior and sneaks past a vampire of my prey's, does my
> prey's vampire tap before the referendum or after it?

After.

Is it really the case that the text "(before resolving the action)" leads to
confusion as to whether it happens before or after resolving the referendum?

> 2) I have a Slaughterhouse in play and bleed successfully. I play
> Scrying of Secrets and look at the top seven cards in my prey's
> library. If I tap a Slaughterhouse now to discard the top two, do I
> then look at the next two (thereby keeping seven in my hand)?

No. You cannot interrupt Scrying to tap the Slaughterhouse. You tap the
Slaughterhouse after Scrying, as you say, so you are no longer looking at those
cards. Scrying resolves when played.

"when resolved" puts it in the "after the pre-resolved" (the "attempting to
block" part -- the part that comes before resolution).

Then the parenthetical specifies the ordering between this during-resolution
effect and the action's during-resolution effect. Namely, that the Faceless
Night during-resolution effect is done first.

> But specifically in this case, I hadn't realized that the referendum's
> resolution was also the action's resolution - I'd thought that the
> action resolved once it wasn't blocked, but before the referendum.
> That clears that up.

Ah, right.

Resolution of a bleed -- burn pool.
Resolution of a hunt -- gain blood.
Resolution of a PA -- conduct a referendum.
Resolution of a Bum's Rush -- conduct a combat.

Exactly correct.
Card text indicates that he is tapped before resolving the action.
So that is when he is tapped.

The part that is confusing to me is: "how can that part be read any other way?"

> Is this because I still don't comprehend what "after the pre-resolved"
> means? 'Cause I don't.

"pre-resolved" : before reaching resolution (i.e., in the blocking window, or in
the post-block pre-resolution window where, say, Conditioning can be played on a
bleed).

Actions have resolutions like strikes have resolutions. The resolution is a
window. The effects of the action are applied in this window. FN's effect also
occurs in this window. These events must be ordered somehow. Card text places
FN's effect before the action's effect. If not for that card text, the player
could choose the order herself.
